Surah 87, "Al-A'la" (The Most High)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.﴾ Declare Him free of whatever does not befit Him. The word "ism" (name) is superfluous (ṣilah), and this is by interpreting "al-A'la" (the Most High) as meaning "al-'uluww" (loftiness), which is domination and power, not loftiness in place. It has also been said: the meaning is "Say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High." In a hadith, when this was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Place it in your prostrations."

Those who sent this in are asking for the translation of a passage from al-Nasafi's Madarik al-Tanzil. The passage is a single tafsir passage on 87:2, so I'll translate it faithfully.

**Translation:**

﴿Who created, then proportioned﴾. That is: He created everything and then made its creation proportioned (tasviyah). He did not bring it forth disjointed and ill-fitting, but in firm arrangement and harmony, and as an indication that it proceeds from a knowing, wise One. Or: He proportioned it according to what contains its benefit and its welfare.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 87, verse 3:

﴿Who determines and then guides.﴾ That is: He determined for every living creature what would suit it, then guided it to it, and made known to it the way to benefit from it. Or the meaning is "and guided, and misguided," but "and misguided" is omitted, by way of *iktifa'* (sufficiency, where one part of a pair is left implicit), like His saying: ﴿He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [Fatir: 8]. "Qadara" (قَدَرَ) and "ʿAliyy" (عَلِيٌّ) are the Arabic words given here as the lexical glosses for the verse.
﴿And He who brings forth the pasturage﴾, He makes grow that which the beasts graze upon.

(p-631) ﴿So He made it a dark, dry stubble﴾: dry and crumbled (hashiman).

﴿Dark﴾ (aḥwā): black. Here "aḥwā" is an attribute (ṣifah) of "ghuthā'an" (stubble).
﴿We shall make you recite, and you will not forget﴾. We shall teach you the Qur'an so that you will not forget it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 87, verse 7:

﴿Except what Allah wills﴾, that He should abrogate it. This is a good tiding from Allah to His Prophet that He will preserve the revelation for him, so that nothing of it slips from him, except what Allah wills to abrogate, so that He removes it from his memory by lifting its ruling and its recitation. Ibn Kaysan the grammarian (al-Nahwi) asked Junayd about it, and he said: "Then you will not forget its practice (al-'amal bihi)." He said: "Someone like you should be taught (yusaddar)." It has also been said: the words "fa-la tansa" (you will not forget) are in the prohibitive mood (al-nahy), and the alif is an added letter for the end of the verse (al-fasila), like His saying "al-sabila" (the way). That is, do not neglect its recitation and its repetition, so that you forget it, except what Allah wills to make you forget by lifting its recitation.

﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and what is hidden﴾. That is: indeed you recite aloud along with the recitation of Jibril, out of fear of losing it, and Allah knows your loudness along with him, and what is in yourself that calls you to speak aloud; or what you recite to yourself out of fear of forgetting. Or He knows what you keep secret and what you make public, of your words and your deeds, and what is apparent and what is concealed of your states.

﴿And We will ease you toward ease﴾, is coordinated with "We will make you recite, so you will not forget" (sanuqri'uka). His saying "Indeed He knows what is spoken aloud and what is hidden" is a parenthetical interjection (i'tiraD). Its meaning: We will grant you success in the method that is easiest and most facile, namely the preservation of the Revelation. It was also said: toward the tolerant Sharia (al-shari'ah al-samhah), which is the easiest of the sharia'as, or: We will grant you success in works that lead to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 87, verse 9:

﴿So remind,﴾ admonish with the Qur'an,

﴿if the reminder benefits﴾. The answer of "in" (the conditional particle "in") is the implied meaning of His words "so remind." It has been said: its apparent form is a condition, and its meaning is a remote likelihood of the reminder having an effect upon them. And it has been said: it is a command to remind in an unrestricted sense, like His words: ﴿So remind; you are only a reminder﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 21], not conditional upon benefit.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 87, verse 10:

﴿He who fears [Allah] will be reminded﴾: he will take heed, and will accept the reminder.

﴿Who fears﴾: [Allah], and the evil consequence [of disbelief].

And he shuns it, keeping away from the reminder, so he does not accept it,

﴿the most wretched﴾: the disbeliever, or the one who is most wretched of the disbelievers, because of his excessive enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was said: it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa.
(p-632) ﴿The one who will burn in the greatest Fire﴾: he enters the Fire of Hell, and "the lesser" is the Fire of this world.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 87, verse 13:

﴿Then he will neither die therein﴾, so that he would find rest from the punishment,

﴿nor will he live﴾, a life in which he would take pleasure. It has been said: "thumma" (then) is used because the wavering between life and death is more dreadful than the burning (al-salyu), so it is remote from it in degrees of severity.

Qad aflaha (﴿Surely he has succeeded﴾): he attained success.

Man tazakka (﴿who purifies himself﴾): he cleansed himself of polytheism (shirk), or he cleansed himself for the prayer (salah), or he paid the zakat. Tazakka is on the pattern tafa''ala, from al-zakah (purification/zakat), like tasaddaqa from al-sadaqah.

ۡ﻿And he remembers the name of his Lord, and says the takbir for opening (the prayer), ﴿and prays﴾, the five (prayers). From this verse, the obligation of the takbir of opening (takbir al-iftitah) is deduced, and that it is not part of the prayer, because the prayer is conjoined to it by a conjunction (fa), which requires difference (between them). It also indicates that opening the prayer is permissible with any of His names, Mighty and Majestic is He. It is related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: "He remembered his return (to Him) and his standing before his Lord, and so he prayed to Him." And it is related from al-Dahhak: "And he remembered the name of his Lord on the way to the place of prayer, and so he prayed the prayer of the Eid."

Ah, I should translate this passage faithfully. Here is the translation:

﴿Nay, you prefer the life of this world﴾ over the Hereafter, so you do not do that by which you would prosper. The one addressed by it is the disbelievers. Its evidence is the recitation of Abu 'Amr: "yu'thirun" (يُؤْثِرُونَ), with the ya' (the third person plural form, "they prefer").
﴿And the Hereafter is better and more enduring.﴾ It is better in itself, and more lasting.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures﴾

"This" (hadha) is a reference to His saying "He has certainly succeeded" (qad aflaha), up to "and more lasting" (abqa), meaning: the meaning of this speech is found in those scriptures. Or it refers to everything in the whole surah. This is evidence for the permissibility of reciting the Qur'an in Persian (al-Farisiyya) during prayer (salah), because He made it mentioned in those scriptures, even though it was not in them with this arrangement (nazm) and in this language (lugha).

The scrolls of Abraham and Moses, ﴿the scrolls of Abraham and Moses﴾, is a *badal* (substitute, or apposition) of "the former scrolls" (al-ṣuḥuf al-ūlā).

In a report: "In the scrolls of Abraham: it behooves the intelligent person to be guardian of his tongue, knowing of his time, and devoted to his affairs."
